resources.string: Enable the accessibility service so the app can react to the current foreground package name and show the navigation overlay for selected apps.
NavXS uses the Android Accessibility Service.
The service is required to display floating navigation buttons over selected apps.
NavXS can detect which app is currently in the foreground.
NavXS uses Accessibility actions: Back, Home and Recent Apps.
NavXS does not read typed text, passwords or message content.
NavXS does not sell or share this data.
Processing is performed solely to provide the navigation overlay feature.
I understand why NavXS needs the Accessibility Service.

The list shows all installed apps on your device. Enable an app to make the NavXS overlay appear whenever it is in the foreground. Use the search bar to filter by name, or toggle Show system apps to include system apps.

Opens a full-screen editor. Drag any active button to exactly where it should sit in the live overlay. Tap a button to select it without moving it. The reset icon restores all default positions. The precision panel moves the selected button by an exact pixel step size.
Tap Back, Home, or Recents to pick a button. All settings below apply to the selected button only.

Use a screenshot as the background to place the buttons exactly where you will need them later.

Pick a screenshot of your app with the image icon and drag the buttons to the spots you want. The slider dims the background so the buttons stay easier to see.

“Reset background” removes the screenshot again. Your button positions are kept.

The screenshot is only a setup aid and is never shown in the normal overlay.
Switches the selected button on or off in the overlay. At least one button must remain active at all times.
Scales the icon relative to its default size.
An optional circle drawn behind the icon to improve visibility on any background.
Fill colour of the background circle.
Diameter of the circle relative to the icon.
0 = hard edge; 100 = fully faded gradient edge.

The tab with the eye icon at the top right of the Design & layout screen slides open a panel showing the selected button on white, grey, and black backgrounds — judge visibility on any app without leaving the screen.
For problems with this app, get support through the issue tracker.
NavXS processes the current foreground package name locally on your device to decide whether the overlay should be shown. No app selection or foreground-app data is sent to external services.
No apps match the current filter.
Drag the selected button to its real overlay position.
At least one button must stay active.
The background image could not be loaded.
Give this app its own buttons, positions and colours. When switched off the default layout is used.
The current values of the target configuration are replaced.
There is no app with its own design and layout yet.

After about 45 seconds without input the button background is hidden and the icon is shown more faintly. A touch immediately restores the configured appearance. This reduces the risk of burn-in but cannot prevent it completely.
Applies to the NavXS user interface only, not to the configured overlay colours.

Every app you enable here also appears in the configuration picker of the Design & layout tab, so you can give it its own buttons later. Disabling an app removes it from that picker again; values you already set for it are kept.

The picker at the top decides which configuration you are editing. Default layout applies to every enabled app that has no configuration of its own. Below it you find all currently enabled apps, sorted by name. After a restart NavXS always starts with Default layout.

This switch appears only when an app is selected. Switched off, the app follows the Default layout and all controls below are shown greyed out with the values that are actually in effect. Switched on, the app gets its own complete design and layout, and only that app is affected by your changes. The first time you switch it on the current Default layout is copied, so nothing changes visually. Switching it off keeps your individual values for later.

Copies a complete design and layout from another configuration into the one you are editing. This is a one-time copy: later changes to the source are not passed on. The current values of the target are replaced, so you are asked to confirm with OK before anything is copied.

Reduces the risk of screen burn-in on OLED displays. After about 45 seconds without input the button background is hidden completely and the icon is shown more faintly, never brighter than the opacity you configured. The first touch immediately restores the configured appearance and still performs the tap. The timer only runs while the real overlay is visible and the screen is on; the preview and the positioning editor are never affected. Your stored button settings are left untouched.

Sets the colour scheme of the NavXS interface itself: System follows the device setting and reacts to changes while the app is running, Light and Dark force one of the two. This never affects the colours you configured for the real overlay buttons.
The background belongs to the configuration you are editing: the default layout and every app with its own design and layout keep their own screenshot and their own opacity.
